label: PF Backlog 439
title: /pf command: build mode only (not orchestrator) + global /pf for all opencode sessions
body:
## Problem / why
The `.opencode/command/pf.md` frontmatter binds every `/pf <verb>` invocation to the `orchestrator` agent (`agent: orchestrator` + `model: opencode-go/mimo-v2.5`), so deterministic thin-client verbs (backlog list, status, ...) run in the orchestrator agent instead of build mode. `.opencode/command/pipeline.md` has the same binding. Also, `/pf` exists only inside the product-forge repo - opencode sessions in other directories have no `/pf` command at all.

## Goal & value
- `/pf ...` always executes in build mode (`agent: build`), with no model pin so the session's model is inherited.
- `/pf ...` available in EVERY opencode session via the global command dir, calling `scripts/pf.py` by absolute path (pf.py self-locates ROOT, so any cwd works).

## In scope / Out of scope
In: frontmatter of `.opencode/command/pf.md` and `.opencode/command/pipeline.md`; new global command `$USERPROFILE/.config/opencode/command/pf.md`. Plus `/pf help [verb]` usage details (help registry + renderer in `scripts/pf.py`).
Out: `scripts/pipeline.py`, agent definitions, and installer (install.py/install.sh/install.bat) wiring.

## User flow
User runs `/pf backlog list` in any opencode session (any cwd) -> command executes under the build agent -> JSON output reported.

## Backend flow (consumed, by id)
`/pf <verb>` -> `scripts/pf.py <verb>` (thin client) -> canonical core/API. No orchestration in the command file (guard: scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py).

## Acceptance criteria (testable G/W/T)
- GIVEN the project `pf.md` WHEN its frontmatter is read THEN `agent: build` is present and `agent: orchestrator` / `model:` are absent.
- GIVEN a session outside the repo WHEN `/pf help` is invoked THEN it resolves to the global command and runs pf.py by absolute path.
- GIVEN `/pf help` WHEN run THEN the overview lists every verb with its usage line (exit 0).
- GIVEN `/pf help <verb>` WHEN run THEN subcommands + flags for that verb are printed (exit 0);
  an unknown topic exits 2 with the verb list.
- GIVEN the repo WHEN `python scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py` runs THEN it exits 0.

## Data model (what is stored, where, owner)
Command frontmatter: `.opencode/command/*.md` (project) and `~/.config/opencode/command/*.md` (global). Single writer: this item's implementation.

## API contract (endpoints and payloads)
None - surface-level change (clients only; API untouched).

## UX (screens / elements / states)
`/pf` slash command available in the command palette of every session.

## Edge cases and errors
- Global vs project command with the same name: project overrides global inside the repo - both are kept in sync at `agent: build`.
- Paths with spaces: absolute pf.py path must be quoted in the global command body.

## Dependencies and links (by id)
BI-PF-0372 (P10 /pf umbrella surface, completed).

## Open questions
None.

## Verification / test plan
python scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py; python -m compileall -q core scripts dashboard; python scripts/dev/wired_audit.py; manual /pf help in a fresh session after opencode restart. python scripts/pf.py help | help backlog | help nope (exit 0/0/2).

delivery.note: merged to develop; precheck PASS (fast, 11 gates) on merge tree

analysis.implementation_strategy: Reuse-first surface change. (1) MODIFY frontmatter of .opencode/command/pf.md and .opencode/command/pipeline.md: set agent: build, remove model: pin and agent: orchestrator. (2) MODIFY scripts/pf.py: add a help registry (verb -> usage line, subcommands, flags) and a renderer for `pf.py help` (overview, exit 0) and `pf.py help <verb>` (details, exit 0; unknown topic -> exit 2 with verb list). Reuse the existing pf.py verb dispatch/ROOT self-location so no path logic is duplicated. (3) NEW file global command $USERPROFILE/.config/opencode/command/pf.md that mirrors the project command but calls pf.py by absolute path (quoted, spaces-safe). Keep bodies in sync with the project command; guard via scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py (extend it to also check the global file and the build-only frontmatter if not already covered). No core/API/agent changes.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0372 (completed) - /pf umbrella surface and scripts/pf.py thin client must exist.
REQUIRES existing scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py guard (from BI-PF-0372 surface work) as the verification gate.
RELATED BI-0178 (per-agent model override) - orthogonal; removing the model: pin means session model inheritance, not the override store.
conflict_findings: Data model declares single writer for .opencode/command/*.md and the global command file for this item - low conflict risk, but any concurrent item touching pf.md frontmatter or pf.py CLI dispatch would conflict; none identified in the current backlog set.
scripts/pf.py is shared surface; if another item extends pf.py verbs concurrently, coordinate the help registry table.
duplication_findings: No existing backlog item covers /pf frontmatter agent binding or global command exposure; BI-PF-0372 (completed) created the /pf umbrella surface, this item is a follow-up adjustment, not duplication.
Candidate existing code (agent_model_override, budget_allocator, cost_model, /api/v1/packaging/build, model-config JSONs) is unrelated to this surface-level change - not reused, not duplicated.
Similar-similar items BI-PF-0336/0337 (api foundation/core APIs) are consumed backends, untouched here.
analysis.rationale: Thin-client verbs must not run under the orchestrator agent; binding to build mode is a small, verifiable frontmatter + CLI-help change with an existing guard script. Adding a global /pf extends reach to all sessions with zero API impact. Classification MODIFY (existing command files + pf.py extended); only the global command md file is new, not a new component. P1: improves correctness and reach of an already-built surface, not a blocker for core flows.
assumptions: opencode resolves project commands over global commands when names collide (stated in edge cases).
pf.py already self-locates ROOT from any cwd (stated in body), so absolute-path invocation from a global command works.
No model: pin in frontmatter means the session's current model/agent model is inherited.
opencode restart is required and acceptable for a new global command to appear (stated in verification).
risks: Global vs project command name collision behavior depends on opencode's resolution order (assumed: project overrides global); verify after opencode restart.

Absolute pf.py path in the global command can break if the repo moves or the user profile path differs per OS ($USERPROFILE is Windows-centric; Linux/macOS is ~/.config/opencode) - spec already targets ~/.config/opencode, acceptable but path derivation should be platform-checked.

Help registry can drift from actual pf.py dispatch table unless generated from or checked against the same source; mitigate by deriving usage strings from a single registry used by dispatch and by extending pf_surface_check.
evidence: Body explicitly states pf.py self-locates ROOT, so any cwd works.
Acceptance criteria include runnable gates: pf_surface_check.py exit 0, pf.py help/help <verb>/help nope exit 0/0/2.
BI-PF-0372 completed provides the existing /pf surface and guard script to extend.
missing_info: Confirm exact opencode global config dir per OS ($USERPROFILE/.config/opencode vs ~/.config/opencode on Linux/macOS) and whether install.py/install.sh/install.bat (out of scope here) will later own copying the global command - who maintains sync between project and global pf.md long-term.
Whether pf_surface_check.py should hard-fail if the global command file is absent on machines where opencode is not installed.

missing: Platform-accurate global opencode command dir (per OS) and long-term sync owner between project and global pf.md.
Decision on whether pf_surface_check.py hard-fails when the global command file is absent.
context_review.reason: All reuse targets (pf.md, pipeline.md, pf.py, pf_surface_check.py) and exit-code contracts are specified; only operational details about the global config path per OS and sync governance require a human decision.

dashboard_impact.reason: Command frontmatter + opencode command file only; no UI surface change.

body_note: Decision: global /pf is SELF-LOCATING (PF_ROOT env -> known checkout -> cwd/parent walk -> clean fail); checked in at .opencode/command_global/pf.md, installed copy must stay byte-identical (pf_surface_check drift guard). install.py/.sh/.bat are NOT wired - they are legacy/unused onboarding scripts, deliberately out of scope.
